thread:
sam_support: FYI — customer AcmeCorp flagged sudden p99 latency spike on /v1/embeddings since 2026-03-15 22:00 UTC. Before: ~1.2s p99, now ~6.5s. Example reqs: req-8a77, req-8a7c. They attached curl + timings.

maria_oncall: @sam_support can you paste a sample curl + headers and any recent deploys? Also which region are they hitting?

sam_support: Region: us-west-2. Sample curl they sent:

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer key-ACME" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"input": "short text", "model": "redwood-embed-xl"}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings

Timing they observe (client-side): 200 reqs -> p50 120ms, p95 320ms, p99 6500ms. Traffic pattern: lots of small, concurrent requests (seq len ~64).

chris_sre: We have matching spikes in infra metrics for us-west-2 starting ~21:45 UTC. p95 up ~2x, p99 up ~5x. No obvious CPU/GPU OOMs. Suspect batching/queueing change or a kernel fallback path for short sequences. Flagging eng-runtime.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-54 - embeddings p99 spike (tags: embeddings, latency, us-west-2)

aya_dev: Repro steps I ran locally to mimic customer:

for i in $(seq 1 200); do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer key-DEV" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"input":"sample text","model":"redwood-embed-xl"}' \n    https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings &
 done; wait

Observed ~1-2% of requests hit 4-7s tail. Logs show large waiting times in batcher queue (queue_ms spiking).

chris_sre: Quick mitigation checklist (prioritized):
1) Apply per-key soft throttle for AcmeCorp (limit to 100 rps)
2) Enable model fallback to redwood-embed-compact (quantized, lower latency)
3) Shorten batching window (20ms -> 5ms) in runtime config for us-west-2
4) Enable prefix cache for repeated prefixes (customer uses same prefix payload)
5) Add circuit-breaker: fail fast on >2.5s backend latency and return 429+Retry-After

maria_oncall: Doing 1 and 2 now. Applying temporary quota to key-ACME and flipping fallback policy to redwood-embed-compact for their key.

sam_support: Customer reports immediate reduction in 5xxs but tail persists. They accept temporary lower-quality model. Asking if we can do anything faster on batcher.

aya_dev: The batching window is a hot config flip: runtime flag --batch-window-ms. I can push change to us-west-2 (hot reload) and watch. Will do a 5ms flip as an experiment.

chris_sre: Also push for an SLO guardrail: automatic fallback when backend p99 > 3s for >5 minutes. Should trigger model fallback + per-key throttle + circuit-breaker. That will reduce blast radius for noisy tenants.

maria_oncall: Flipped model fallback and quota at 23:02 UTC. Pushed batch-window flip at 23:10 UTC for us-west-2 to 5ms. Telemetry after flip: p99 dropped from ~6.5s -> ~2.1s. Still above our target SLO (1.5s) but much better. Keeping both mitigations active.

chris_sre: Suggested permanent mitigation items for eng-runtime:
- Investigate kernel selection path for short sequences that appears to fall back to a high-latency kernel.
- Add telemetry on "queue_ms" split by sequence-length buckets.
- Add automatic batch-window autoscaling that shrinks for high-concurrency, short-seq workloads.

aya_dev: Noted. I can add a quick metric on seq-length buckets and an alert for queue_ms p99 by bucket.

maria_oncall: We'll keep monitoring. If p99 rises >3s again, we'll escalate to SEV and consider rolling back the 2026-03-15 batcher heuristic change (deployed 21:30 UTC).

sam_support: Action items: support to keep AcmeCorp updated (they want daily updates), eng-runtime (aya_dev) to create a follow-up ticket with repro + kernel traces, eng-sre (chris_sre) to author the SLO guardrail (p99 trigger -> automatic fallbacks/cb), and oncall to keep the temporary guardrails until fix.

chris_sre: Suspected root cause: the 21:30 deploy changed batcher heuristics and introduced a code path that triggers a synchronous kernel for short sequences under certain contention. Prioritize targeted revert or fix.

maria_oncall: Monitoring shows stabilization but we'll leave mitigations in place overnight. Will update account team and close incident if stable for 6 hours.

sam_support: Thanks all — great coordinated response :thumbsup:
